title: Career Roadmap · Carpenter
summary: A Carpenter measures, cuts, shapes and assembles wood and engineered boards to create furniture, doors, windows, cabinets, interiors and construction fittings.

blocks.text: Primary pathway
Core work
Technical drawings • Measuring and marking • Cutting and joining • Furniture making • Door and window fitting • Site installation.

blocks.label: Recommended
blocks.text: Class 10; check the chosen ITI trade’s entry requirements.

blocks.label: Stream
blocks.text: Science in Classes 11–12 can be useful but is not always required for ITI entry.

blocks.label: Admission
blocks.text: State ITI counselling or institute-specific admission.

blocks.label: Explore
blocks.text: Furniture design, woodworking, interior fit-outs, construction carpentry and cabinetmaking.

blocks.label: Early skills
blocks.text: Measurement, geometry, spatial reasoning, drawing interpretation and safe tool handling.

blocks.text: Class 10 → Relevant diploma or recognized vocational program → Furniture production, interior installation or construction-related roles, subject to course eligibility.

blocks.label: Stage 1 — Foundation
blocks.text: Workshop safety, measuring, marking, wood types, hand tools and technical drawings.

blocks.label: Stage 2 — Core skills
blocks.text: Cutting, planing, drilling, joints, fastening, sanding and basic furniture assembly.

blocks.label: Stage 3 — Advanced skills
blocks.text: Cabinetmaking, doors and windows, modular furniture, installation, finishing and CNC woodworking.

blocks.label: Stage 4 — Career preparation
blocks.text: Build a project portfolio, practise estimating materials, gain workshop experience and apply for apprenticeships.

blocks.label: Project ideas
blocks.text: Make a small wooden stool • Build a simple shelf • Assemble a door frame • Create a storage cabinet using a measured drawing.

blocks.label: Government / public sector
blocks.text: Public works maintenance units, railway workshops and eligible government furniture / maintenance workshops.

blocks.label: Private sector
blocks.text: Furniture factories, modular-kitchen firms, interior contractors, door-and-window manufacturers and carpentry workshops.

blocks.label: Ideal training areas
blocks.text: Furniture assembly • Interior fit-outs • Joinery • Site installation.
Search Apprenticeship India. Openings, eligibility and stipend depend on the employer and official notification.

blocks.label: Self-employment route
blocks.text: Practical experience → Independent carpentry / furniture service business.

blocks.label: Further education
blocks.text: Eligible diploma in Civil Engineering, interior design or furniture-related studies → broader design, site or production roles.
Relevant training

blocks.label: Institutions to investigate
blocks.text: Government ITIs, NSTIs, state polytechnics, recognized skill centres and employer training facilities. Verify each program’s current status and entry criteria.

blocks.label: Industries
blocks.text: Residential and commercial construction, furniture manufacturing, interior design, hospitality, retail fixtures and property maintenance.

blocks.label: Technical skills
blocks.text: Measurement, marking, wood cutting, joinery, assembly, drawing interpretation, material estimation, installation and safe tool handling.

blocks.label: Tools / technologies
blocks.text: Hand saws, chisels, drills, planers, routers, sanders, measuring tools, CAD software and CNC woodworking machines.
Useful credentials

items.text: CAD or CNC woodworking training from a recognized provider.
Workplace safety and finishing training relevant to the job.

blocks.label: Countries to explore
blocks.text: Australia, Canada, Germany, UK and New Zealand.

blocks.text: Relevant education or experience, practical assessment where applicable, language proficiency and study documentation. Recognition and licensing requirements vary by destination.

blocks.text: Carpenter, Joiner, Cabinetmaker, Furniture Maker and Interior Fit-out Technician.
